To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the improved pyruvate utilization of the BFDC variant is due to a decrease in the rate of formation of the acetaldehyde-enzyme complex and an increase in the rate of the subsequent hydrolysis of the complex.

the BFDC T37L/A460Y mutant has a 10,000 fold increased preference for pyruvade as a substrate over benzoylformiate compared to wtBFDC and that the increased pyruvade utilization is due to a decrease in the rate constant for the decarboxylation step of pyruvade and an increase in the rate constant of the decarboxylating step of benzoylformiade.
a single amino acid replacement in the active site of a thiamin dipyhosphate-dependent enzyme can dramatically change its substrate specificity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of enzymes that are capable of catalyzing reactions that are currently not accessible by natural enzymes, such as the decarboxylation and decarbonylation of aromatic 2-ketoacids.
understanding how substrate specificity of a thiamin dipyhosphate-dependent enzyme can be modulated by rational design.
the development of a novel biocatalyst that has the potential to replace chemical processes in the production of benzaldehyde and pyruvates.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
BFDC T377A/A460Y is a pyruvate-benzoylformic acid decarboxylating enzyme.
the BFDC T37L/A460Y mutation increases the rate-limiting step of the pyruvate reaction, which is consistent with the observed decrease in the k cat value for benzoyloformate.

the BFDC T37L/A460Y mutation increases the rate of the first catalytic step (deprotonation of the thiazolium C-2 atom) for pyruvatedehydrated intermediate (PDH) formation and decreases the rate of the last catalytic step (hydrolysis of the acetyl thiazolium intermediate (ATI)) for the benzoylformatedehydrate intermediate (BFDH) to benzaldehyde.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

BFDC T377A/L460Y is a hybrid between the wtBFDC and PDC, with the T377L substitution increasing the affinity of the enzyme for pyruvatedehydrate and the A460Y substitution decreasing the affinity of the active site for benzoyl formate.
the BFDC T37L/A460Y mutant has evolved to have a greater affinity for pyruvade, but a lower rate of decarboxylation, compared to wtBFDC.

the BFDC T371L/A460Y double mutant exhibits an increase of the pyruvate to benzoylformrate conversion ratio of about 10,000, which is due to (i) a decrease in the rate-limiting step for pyruvates conversion, (ii) an increase in the rate-limit of the benzoylformic acid conversion and (iii) a decrease in kcat for benzoyl formic acid conversion.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the BFDC T37L/A460Y enzyme is a hybrid between the BFDC and PDC enzymes, with a BFDC-like active site and a PDC-like substrate specificity.
the BFDC T37L/A460Y mutation results in a significant change in the binding of the 2-keto acid substrates, with pyruvates binding in a more open conformation than the benzoylformates.
the BFDC T37L/A460Y mutant has a lower barrier for the first chemical step of the reaction (deprotonation of the substrate) and a higher barrier for the first proton-transfer step of the reaction.
